answer: Scarce Label Ledger. Each agent carries a persistent jade token whose ID is derived from a scarce, sequentially issued resource; the ledger publishes every token's issue order and lineage. Registering a duplicate forces a visible fork: two tokens claim the same predecessor slot, which is logged and flagged automatically. An attacker must acquire a fresh scarce slot per identity, so cost scales linearly with each duplicate and leaves an audit trail. Honest agents see an oasis of clean lineage; sybils create noisy echo patterns that reviewers can trace.
